tier_reason: docs/PERFORMANCE.md tabulates first-party Criterion medians from the 0.6.0 release for sigilbuzz vs rustybuzz 0.20 (bench code public in benches/shape_{latin,arabic,devanagari,khmer,hebrew}.rs), but rustc version and CPU model are not stated (only 'macOS arm64 workstation'), so it cannot be A; there is no independent measurement and no HarfBuzz measurement at all.

corrections.baseline: rustybuzz 0.20 (archived Rust port of HarfBuzz) only; HarfBuzz itself and FreeType are never measured, and the sigilbuzz-capi hb_* C library is never benchmarked against libharfbuzz
corrections.claimed_speedup: Against rustybuzz only, faster on two of five scripts: Latin 11.39 us vs 15.03 us (page ratio 0.76x, about 1.32x faster, derived from page data) and Hebrew 10.99 us vs 17.28 us (page ratio 0.64x, about 1.57x faster, derived from page data). Slower on the other three: Arabic 290 us vs 108 us (2.70x slower), Devanagari 419 us vs 85.8 us (4.89x slower), Khmer 91.6 us vs 49.0 us (1.87x slower). No HarfBuzz comparison exists, so no win over HarfBuzz is shown.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench with Criterion; current Cargo.toml bench profile inherits release (lto = thin, codegen-units = 1, panic = abort, debug = true); rustc version not stated (MSRV 1.81). The table dates from 0.6.0 (2026-04-24), before the 0.22.0 move to Criterion 0.8, so the exact settings used for these numbers are not stated.
corrections.hardware: maintainer's macOS arm64 workstation; CPU model not stated
corrections.workload: Each Criterion bench shapes one fixed ~200-codepoint string per script through sigilbuzz and rustybuzz 0.20 back to back with no explicit features (font defaults such as liga and kern apply), face parsed once outside the loop and a fresh buffer per iteration: Latin on Open Sans, Arabic on Amiri (RTL), Devanagari on Noto Sans Devanagari, Khmer on Noto Sans Khmer, Hebrew on Noto Sans Hebrew (RTL). Medians from the 0.6.0 release.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars, 0 forks; crates.io crate first published 2026-10-02 (0.22.0), 0.23.0 published 2026-10-03, 55 downloads
corrections.caveats: No HarfBuzz win is shown: the only baseline is rustybuzz 0.20, and the sigilbuzz-capi drop-in hb_* library is never timed against libharfbuzz. rustybuzz's own README says it is 1.5-2x slower than HarfBuzz and that the project is archived in favour of HarfRust, so even the Latin and Hebrew wins (1.32x and 1.57x over rustybuzz) do not imply parity with HarfBuzz, and the 1.9x-4.9x losses on Arabic, Devanagari and Khmer suggest sigilbuzz is well behind HarfBuzz on complex scripts (inference, not measured). Numbers are first-party, from one unnamed Apple arm64 machine and one ~200-codepoint string per script, and date from 0.6.0 (2026-04-24) while the current release is 0.23.0; PERFORMANCE.md has not been refreshed since, and the CHANGELOG quotes slightly different ratios for the same run (Devanagari 4.98x, Arabic 2.72x, Khmer 1.88x). The crate is pure Rust; C and C++ use goes through the sigilbuzz-capi crate (cargo-c build). The repo has 0 stars and the crate was first published on 2026-10-02. Kept as a C-callable HarfBuzz-API alternative with an honest, mixed comparison against a HarfBuzz port, not as a faster-than-HarfBuzz library.

notes: No HarfBuzz comparison exists anywhere in the repo (README, docs/PERFORMANCE.md, CHANGELOG, benches/); the page does compare against the record's named baseline, rustybuzz, with a mixed result, so this is a keep-and-document entry, not a reject. Language is Rust (pure-Rust core, C ABI via crates/sigilbuzz-capi exporting hb_* symbols); 'language' is not a correctable field, so set it via decisions.json if a different label is wanted. Repo history starts 2026-04-24 (0.1.0) per CHANGELOG; 546 commits on main.

tier_reason: PR #2 and PR #3 give first-party before/after timings against the repo's own pre-PR master (-O2, x86-64, mean of 40 runs and best of 11 runs), but no benchmark harness is in the repo (example/ holds only example1.c, example2.c and SVGs), and neither compiler version nor CPU model is stated; C.

corrections.baseline: The fork's own pre-PR master, not a category incumbent: a 2024-08-15 copy of memononen/nanosvg whose rasterizer matches upstream nanosvgrast.h apart from later upstream fixes (paint order, NaN clamping, dash stroke preparation). Skia, Cairo and Blend2D are not measured, and upstream nanosvg HEAD is not measured either.
corrections.claimed_speedup: PR #2 vs pre-PR master (mean of 40 runs, -O2, x86-64): rasterization 2.5x-3.7x faster per the PR text (23.svg 1x 15.5 ms to 5.6 ms; 23.svg 3x 83.4 ms to 24.3 ms; drawing.svg 1x 8.7 ms to 3.4 ms; drawing.svg 3x 85.8 ms to 31.4 ms; nano.svg 1x 1.29 ms to 0.35 ms; nano.svg 3x 10.8 ms to 2.9 ms; per-row ratios 2.56x-3.72x, derived from page data), parsing up to about 2x (23.svg 3x 1.17 ms to 0.65 ms). PR #3 on top of that (best of 11 runs, callgrind instruction counts): 1.34x-1.98x (23.svg 1x 3.90 ms to 2.91 ms; 23.svg 3x 19.1 ms to 11.1 ms; drawing.svg 1x 2.49 ms to 1.49 ms; drawing.svg 3x 25.9 ms to 17.6 ms; nano.svg 3x 2.79 ms to 1.85 ms; gradients 3x 4.64 ms to 2.34 ms), output byte-identical to the post-PR #2 master; with NSVG_NO_SIMD the gain mostly disappears (e.g. 23.svg 3x 17.2 ms). The two PRs were timed under different conditions (PR #3's master time for 23.svg 3x, 19.1 ms, is below PR #2's optimized 24.3 ms), so the speedups should not be multiplied.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O2 on x86-64; compiler and version not stated (PR #3 says the SSE2 path enables on GCC, Clang and MSVC)
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the fork's own earlier code, not a recognisable category incumbent: no Skia, Cairo or Blend2D numbers, and no run against upstream memononen/nanosvg HEAD (the pre-PR rasterizer is a 2024 snapshot of upstream minus some later upstream fixes, so the gain over upstream is inferred). No harness or benchmark script is in the repo and no CPU or compiler version is given. All optimization commits were authored by an account named 'claude' on branch claude/friendly-ride-r2z9m7 and merged by the owner (milostosic) on 2026-09-24 (PR #2 opened by claude; PR #3 shown as opened by milostosic). PR #2 also fixes a defringe bug, so its output is not byte-identical to the old master in the first row and column. The README, inherited from upstream, still says the rasterizer is 'not particular fast or accurate' and that the project 'is not actively maintained'. Not a GitHub fork: a standalone copy (initial commit 2024-08-15) carrying Mikko Mononen's zlib license; 0 stars.
corrections.workload: Parsing and rasterizing example/23.svg, drawing.svg, nano.svg and a gradient test SVG at 1x and 3x scale with the single-header NanoSVG rasterizer, before and after each PR.

notes: No harness and no machine: the PRs state only -O2, x86-64 and run counts. The baseline is not a recognisable incumbent but the fork's own past, which a diff shows is essentially upstream NanoSVG's 2024 rasterizer; I kept it at C as a keep-and-document entry rather than rejecting, since NanoSVG itself is a known library, but if the orchestrator treats own-past baselines as no comparison the reject reason would be no-baseline-comparison. Speedup range corrected to the PR's own 2.5x-3.7x.

tier_reason: The benchmark code is public (vignettes/ragg_performance.Rmd, bench::mark per device against png(type='cairo') with antialias none/gray/subpixel), but results exist only as ridge plots in the rendered article, built on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 runner with no CPU model or compiler flags stated, and the ~33%/40% figures are first-party summary prose; C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Faster (up to 40% faster than anti-aliased cairo device)'; no number in the vignette backs the 40%. Vignette conclusion: 'a general speed gain of around ~33% compared to cairo' among anti-aliased devices. Rendered plots (pkgdown build of 2026-04-08), read approximately: complex ggplot2 composite ragg about 245 ms vs anti-aliased cairo (gray and subpixel) about 320-325 ms, about 1.3x (derived from page data, plot readings), with the void_dev() non-rendering baseline at about 130 ms; unfilled circles about 5.5 ms vs about 7.3 ms; filled complex polygon about 38 ms vs about 48 ms. Non-anti-aliased cairo beats ragg on single primitives (about 3.1 ms unfilled circles, about 6.5 ms filled polygon) but is slower on the composite (about 265 ms). Cairo is about twice as fast to open and close a device, slightly faster for non-rotated rasters, and about on par for gradients; ragg is clearly faster for clipping paths, masks and patterns.
corrections.hardware: GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 runner (pkgdown article build of 2026-04-08: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, R 4.5.3, ragg 1.5.2 per session info); CPU model not stated
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated (package built on the CI runner with R's default toolchain and flags; session info lists no compiler)
corrections.license: MIT; bundled AGG 2.4 sources under a BSD-style license (LICENSE.note)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 184 stars, 30 forks; on CRAN; README documents use as a knitr device (dev = 'ragg_png') and as the RStudio AGG graphics backend
corrections.workload: R graphics primitives (1000 random points with pch 1, 19, 4, 0, 15, 2 and '#', lines with and without dash patterns, polygons, even-odd paths, rotated and interpolated rasters, text strings), a prebuilt layered ggplot2 plot (hexbin, points, smooth, facets) and grid clipping paths, masks, gradients and patterns, rendered to PNG and timed with bench::mark (min_iterations 10) per device: agg_png() vs png(type = 'cairo') with antialias none, gray and subpixel; void_dev() time marks non-rendering overhead; Xlib omitted on the build machine.
corrections.caveats: Language mismatch with the C++ filter: ragg is an R package. Its C++ core (src/ragg.h includes Rinternals.h and R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h) implements R's graphics-device API and cannot be called from plain C++ without R; the reusable C++ piece is the bundled AGG 2.4 rasterizer. Baseline is R's cairo device (grDevices png(type = 'cairo')), not Cairo called from C++, and both sides include R graphics-engine overhead. Numbers are first-party and shown only as ridge plots from a CI runner (no CPU model, no compiler flags); the README's 'up to 40%' has no backing figure and the vignette's '~33%' is summary prose. Gains are smallest on fills because grDevices cairo does not anti-alias fills; non-anti-aliased cairo is faster on single primitives, and cairo is about twice as fast to open/close a device and slightly faster on non-rotated rasters. The vignette is excluded from the CRAN tarball (.Rbuildignore) and rendered only on the pkgdown site; the rendered copy is on the gh-pages branch.

notes: Benchmark code is the R script in vignettes/ragg_performance.Rmd; the machine is a GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 runner per the rendered article's session info (raw.githubusercontent.com gh-pages copy, since ragg.r-lib.org is blocked), CPU model unstated. Language should be 'R (C++ core on AGG 2.4)' via a decisions.json override, since 'language' is not a correctable field; the C++ filter mismatch is in caveats. CRAN was blocked (403), so CRAN usage figures were not checked.
